thread:
Maya K: Heads-up — proposing a small, additive change to /reorder to help routing+telemetry for tenant-level soft quotas. sketch below.
Samir: 🙏 show the sketch, curious how this avoids breaking existing clients.
Maya K: Idea: add an optional top-level field `routing_hint` and a telemetry-only `units_consumed_hint`. both optional and ignored by old servers/clients. example payload:
```json
{
  "queries": [...],
  "routing_hint": "dedicated:low-latency",
  "units_consumed_hint": 12
}
```
Samir: That `routing_hint` feels like a hint that could be abused. who enforces?
Liam O'Connor: +1 on enforcement question. If we treat it as pure hint for the router it might be OK, but we need a fallback path. Also worried about cache/kv reuse if hint mismatches actual model used.
Rachel P: telemetry concern: Console currently shows per-route tokens and latency. We have no visibility into per-tenant model fallback events. If we start accepting hints we need new telemetry signals: `hint_accepted`, `hint_overridden_reason`, `actual_model` — otherwise ops can't interpret quotas.
Maya K: Agreed. My proposal includes emitting a structured trace event on each request with fields: model_hint, model_selected, routing_bucket, units_charged. Those are only emitted when the client opt-in header `X-RW-Telemetry: v1` is present.
Samir: Opt-in header seems reasonable for privacy. But how do we compute `units_charged`? That ties directly into billing/quotas and is dangerous as a client-provided hint.
Maya K: `units_consumed_hint` is only a hint for routing decisions (eg. so router can decide to route heavy requests to dedicated pools). We never use it for billing — billing reads actual tokens from the runtime. The hint is solely to improve scheduling.
Liam O'Connor: Then we must make the console show both `units_hint` and `units_actual` side-by-side. Also add an alert if they diverge by > 2x for a tenant for a day.
Rachel P: UX question: how do we present canary rollouts for this change? We need a way for teams to toggle hint-respecting routing per-route in the Console and run canaries to ensure it doesn't degrade latency.
Maya K: Proposed rollout plan: default off for all tenants. Add per-route toggle in Console -> Routing settings: "Respect client routing hints". Allow canary by percentage + duration. The server will log `hint_mode = {off, log-only, enforce}`.
Samir: Sounds good. A few edge cases: 1) multi-candidate reorders where candidates require different models; 2) what if hint directs to a model that's behind a quota or down? 3) how to handle cross-tenant isolation?
Maya K: For (1) router can expand to model fanout when needed and still surface `model_selected` list. For (2) router returns a stable fallback and emits `hint_overridden_reason = capacity|health|quota`. For (3) routing_hint is honored only when tenant has dedicated affinity — otherwise ignored. We'll document that.
Liam O'Connor: Telemetry/DB cost: storing per-request structured events could blow up ingestion. We should sample traces (1% by default) and have a higher sampling for tenants with active toggles.
Rachel P: Console needs aggregated metrics: hint acceptance rate, hint override reasons, avg latency by hint vs no-hint, and a small timeline of incidents when hint_overridden_reason spiked. Ops can use this to rollback.
Samir: API shape change debate: instead of adding fields into request body, could we expose a small request header `X-RW-Routing: dedicated=low-latency;units=12` so we avoid payload churn?
Maya K: I prefer body fields for visibility and easier SDK mapping. Headers are fine but harder to surface in SDK typed clients. Both are doable — we can support both, body takes precedence.
Devex Bot: FYI: sdk-js and sdk-py will need minor bump if we add body fields. Docs PR should include examples for both header and body ways.
Maya K: On scoring/response shape — we should extend the response to include per-candidate `model_version` and `units_charged` (stringified ints) so clients can reconcile. Example response fragment:
```json
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "c1",
      "score": 0.812,
      "model_version": "rw-v2.1",
      "units_charged": 4
    }
  ]
}
```
Samir: Adding `units_charged` per-candidate could be noisy but I like it for debugging. Make it optional in response and gated by `X-RW-Telemetry` header.
Liam O'Connor: Also discuss score formats: we currently return raw logits for some endpoints and normalized probabilities for others. For reorder we should standardize: `score` = normalized [0,1] float; and add `score_raw` only when `explain=raw` is requested. Keeps console charts sane.
Maya K: Agree. Standardization reduces misinterpretation in dashboards. We'll document normalization function (softmax across this candidate set unless scorer marks `absolute_score: true`).
Rachel P: Dashboard UI asks: when model selection changes mid-fanout, how to attribute latency and cost? We should introduce `attribution` view that marks primary model per-request and secondary per-candidate. This helps billing reconciliation and SLO attribution.
Samir: Ops automation: add an alert if tenant's hint-acceptance correlates with latency regressions (>10th percentile change) over 1h. Also track error spikes when `hint_mode=enforce`.
Maya K: Implementation plan: 1) runtime: accept hint fields (no-op if not present), emit trace events; 2) router: consult hint when tenant has affinity and hint_mode != off; 3) console: add toggle + metrics + canary flow; 4) SDKs/docs + migrations.
Liam O'Connor: Backwards compat test matrix: old clients -> new router; new clients -> old router; new clients -> new router. Need non-regression for each.
Rachel P: PM ask: can we ship a soft-launch to internal tenants first? infra-bot can we gate toggles to `redwood-internal` workspace?
infra-bot: Toggle gating created: `routing_hint_experiment` ring = internal -> beta -> public. Use feature-flag key rw.routing_hint_experiment.
Maya K: Thanks infra-bot. I'll put up a tiny API RFC and link SDK patches. Any objections to proceeding with a narrow opt-in pilot next week?
Samir: No objections, please include the sampling plan for telemetry so we don't OOM ES.
Liam O'Connor: +1, and add a rollback playbook in the Console for the toggle.
Rachel P: I'll draft the Console screens and mockups today.
Maya K: Great — I'll circulate the RFC and PRs. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
